intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene on chromosome 10.

paragraphs.text: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is a rare disorder of CoQ10 biosynthesis caused by defects in prenyldiphosphate synthase subunit 1 (PDSS1), the human ortholog of yeast COQ1. The clinical picture varies. Some patients have sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, with mild intellectual disability, muscle weakness, and cardiac valvulopathy. Others have a severe early-onset multisystem disease with encephalopathy, nephrotic syndrome or pulmonary hypertension, and death in early childhood (Mollet et al., 2007; Nardecchia et al., 2021; Bellusci et al., 2021).

checks.claim: COQ10D2 is a rare disorder of CoQ10 biosynthesis caused by defects in prenyldiphosphate synthase subunit 1 (PDSS1).
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified 2 novel inborn errors of CoQ10 biosynthesis in 2 distinct families.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a CoQ10 biosynthesis defect caused by a PDSS1 mutation, but it does not call the disorder rare.

paragraphs.text: Mollet et al. (2007) reported a family (family 1) with an inborn error of CoQ10 biosynthesis. As summarized by Nardecchia et al. (2021), the 2 affected sibs in this family were a 22-year-old male and a 14-year-old female. Both had neurosensorial deafness, optic atrophy, mild intellectual disability, muscular weakness, and mild to moderate valvulopathy. Hearing loss developed before the optic atrophy. Both sibs also had lactic acidosis, macrocephaly, peripheral neuropathy, obesity, and livedo reticularis. Brain MRI was not performed.

paragraphs.text: Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported 2 sisters born to consanguineous Egyptian parents. The older sister, aged 16 years, walked independently at 15 months but had severe language delay. At age 4 years she was found to have profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, and mild intellectual disability was diagnosed later. Her visual acuity was normal at 11 years but 1/10 bilaterally at 14 years, with red-green dyschromatopsia. Fundus examination showed optic atrophy that was most marked in the inferior temporal sector. Visual evoked potentials showed increased latency and reduced amplitude of the P100 waveform, and optical coherence tomography showed bilateral thinning of the retinal nerve fiber layer. She also had diffuse mild muscle weakness and mild postural tremor of the upper limbs. Brain MRI was normal. Echocardiography showed a moderately dysplastic mitral valve with moderate insufficiency, medium-grade tricuspid insufficiency with an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 40 mm Hg, and a moderately dilated left atrium. Her 6-year-old sister had bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. At age 6 years she developed decreased visual acuity, with optic atrophy (bilateral temporal pallor of the optic nerve head) and divergent strabismus. In both sisters, sensorineural deafness came before the optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Bellusci et al. (2021) reported a boy, born prematurely after an in vitro fertilization twin pregnancy complicated by twin-twin transfusion. At 5 months of age he had failure to thrive, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, bilateral hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, and chronic distal phalangeal erythema. Laboratory tests showed anemia, lactic acidosis, 3-methylglutaconic and tricarboxylic aciduria, and decreased CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes. He went on to develop a progressive multisystem disorder with severe developmental delay, pyramidal dysfunction, seizures, tremor, optic atrophy, nystagmus, severe visual and hearing impairment, and chronic heart failure. Brain MRI showed mild cerebral atrophy at 12 months. At 24 months it showed cystic change in the white matter, with small necrotic or porencephalic cysts around the lateral ventricles and in the commissural fibers. He died at age 3 years. The authors proposed that the combination of phalangeal erythema, livedo reticularis, and pulmonary hypertension pointed to microvascular dysfunction.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sisters with sensorineural deafness and optic atrophy born to consanguineous Egyptian parents, Nardecchia et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing and identified a homozygous c.735G-T transversion in the PDSS1 gene, resulting in a gln245-to-his (Q245H) substitution at a highly conserved position. Sanger sequencing of OPA1, OPA3, and WFS1 had found no pathogenic variants. The PDSS1 variant was absent from gnomAD and lay within a 12-Mb region of homozygosity. Both parents were heterozygous. Among the unaffected sibs, 1 was homozygous wildtype and 1 was heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency (family 1), Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous asp308-to-glu (D308E) mutation in the PDSS1 gene, affecting a conserved residue. Nardecchia et al. (2021) gave the nucleotide change as c.924T-G. paragraphs.text: In 2 sisters with sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, born to consanguineous Egyptian parents, Nardecchia et al. (2021) identified a homozygous c.735G-T transversion in the PDSS1 gene by whole-exome sequencing, resulting in a gln245-to-his (Q245H) substitution at a highly conserved position. The variant was absent from gnomAD and lay within a 12-Mb region of homozygosity. Both parents were heterozygous. Among the unaffected sibs, 1 was homozygous wildtype and 1 was heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: In a boy with primary CoQ10 deficiency, Bellusci et al. (2021) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the PDSS1 gene: a c.716T-G transversion resulting in a val239-to-gly (V239G) substitution, and a c.1183C-T transition resulting in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution. His features included hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, distal phalangeal erythema, lactic acidosis, and 3-methylglutaconic aciduria. He died at age 3 years.
